results.title: Model Context Protocol - Introduction
results.text: The Model Context Protocol (MCP) is an open protocol that standardizes how applications provide context to large language models. MCP provides a standardized way to connect AI models to different data sources and tools, and follows a client-host-server architecture.

results.title: Introducing the Model Context Protocol
results.author: Anthropic
results.text: Today we are open-sourcing the Model Context Protocol (MCP), a new standard for connecting AI assistants to the systems where data lives. MCP addresses the fragmentation caused by bespoke integrations and is available as an open specification with reference SDKs.
results.summary: Anthropic open-sources MCP, a standard for connecting assistants to external data.

results.title: A Survey of the Model Context Protocol for Tool-Using Agents
results.author: L. Chen, R. Kapoor, et al.
results.text: We survey the Model Context Protocol and compare it with prior tool-use interfaces such as OpenAI function calling and LangChain tools, covering security, discovery and lifecycle management for tool-using agents.
results.summary: A survey comparing MCP with earlier tool-use interfaces for LLM agents.
